prerequisites: Knowledge of the contents of Mechanics, Strength of Materials, Theory of Structures (or the Theory of Structures course from the first semester of the Master's), and Design and Calculation of Structures.

learning_outcomes.text: Students should know how to apply acquired knowledge and problem-solving skills in new or unfamiliar environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their field of study

Students should be able to integrate knowledge and face the complexity of formulating judgments based on incomplete or limited information, including reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments
Students should know how to communicate their conclusions and the knowledge and ultimate reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences in a clear and unambiguous way
Students should possess learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a largely self-directed or autonomous way

Have adequate knowledge of the scientific and technological aspects of: mathematical, analytical and numerical methods in engineering, electrical engineering, energy engineering, chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, continuum mechanics, industrial electronics, automation, manufacturing, materials, quantitative management methods, industrial informatics, urban planning and infrastructures.
Project, calculate and design products, processes, installations and plants.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Engineer.
Knowledge and skills for the calculation and design of structures.
Design and calculate structures with articulated and rigid nodes
Design, model and calculate a simple industrial structure.
Apply basic design criteria for industrial facilities according to the planned operating conditions.
Know and correctly interpret the meaning and scope of applicable regulations and instructions

syllabus_topics: Systems of one degree of freedom.
Systems of N degrees of freedom.

assessment_methods.method: Attendance to Laboratory Practices and submission of Practice Report (P2)

assessment_rules: For ordinary evaluation with laboratory practices and reports, a minimum grade of 4/10 is required for both the written exam (P1) and the practice report (P2). If all minimums are met and attendance to practical classes is 85% or higher, the final grade is calculated as 0.7 * P1 + 0.3 * P2; otherwise, the grade will be the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0. The extraordinary evaluation follows the same criteria, with the attendance and reports from the semester being validated. For students in differentiated evaluation or without laboratory practices/reports, the evaluation consists of a written exam (P1) and a practice exam (P2) (evaluating knowledge related to laboratory practical classes, including software use), each requiring a minimum of 4/10, and the final grade is calculated as 0.7 * P1 + 0.3 * P2, or the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0 if minimums are not met.
